messages:
maya: quick heads-up — did a 48h continuous-batching profile against canary with KV prefetch enabled. seeing a sharp OOM spike when batch growth crosses ~1.7x baseline. attaching short summary below.

maya: TL;DR: padding blowup from unexpected seq growth + workspace fragmentation during kernel switch. not a single catastrophic leak, more of an amortized accounting problem.

maya: Key numbers (aggregated):
```
- baseline (no prefetch): median batch_size 12, pad_waste ~6%, mem_per_request 420MB
- with prefetch heur: median batch_size 19, pad_waste ~22%, mem_per_request 610MB
- OOM rate: 0 -> 3.4/hr on canary cluster over 48h
```

sanjiv: interesting. do we have per-seq distribution? is growth coming from a few long tails or broad shift?

maya: distribution shifted: p95 length moved from 256->324, p99 from 512->640. so both tail and median drift. prefetch seems to grab KV entries early which increases effective seq for padding heuristics.

liam: that explains kernel selection churn — kernels that assume shorter seq get chosen then we switch and reallocate workspace, causing fragmentation. any logs showing allocator churn?

maya: posted allocator snapshot (small).
```
[alloc-snap]
free_slabs: 8 -> 3 over 30m
largest_free_chunk: 1.2GB -> 420MB
reclaimed_pages: 120k
workspaces_in_use: 24 -> 38
oom_stack: runtime::serve::dispatch -> allocator::reserve_workspace
```

arjun: thanks. two quick ideas: 1) cap prefetch activation when avg_batch_growth > 1.4x 2) opportunistic buffer reuse on kernel switch (try to map new kernel into existing workspace if size delta < 20%).

zoe: +1 for reuse. we already have a small cache of released buffers but it's keyed by exact size. making it size-classed (20% buckets) could reduce churn without huge complexity.

sanjiv: also suggest adding a safety margin to workspace sizing when kernel switch frequency > X per minute. if kernels flip frequently, we should size for the larger kernel to avoid repeated reallocs.

maya: prototyped two experiments on canary: A) prefetch-throttle when growth>1.5x, B) size-class reuse with 25% buckets.

maya: results (24h):
```
- experiment A: batch median back to 13, pad_waste 8%, OOM rate 0.4/hr (majority transient)
- experiment B: batch median 17, pad_waste 11%, OOM rate 0.2/hr, allocator churn lowered by 60%
- combined A+B: batch median 14, pad_waste 7%, OOM rate 0.05/hr, 90% drop in workspace reallocs
```

liam: sweet. any perf regression on throughput/latency from reuse?

maya: 95th latency stable; throughput improved slightly because less time in reserve/alloc path. memory headroom improved by ~18%.

arjun: what's the implementation risk for size-classed reuse? sounds straightforward but watch for fragmentation inside big buckets. maybe add LRU eviction for largest objects.

zoe: I'll prototype a bucketed freelist w/ atomic lists per bucket and a simple fallback to direct alloc. low-risk change.

sanjiv: we should also add a new metric: `workspace_reallocs_per_min` and an alert if > 5/min during steady-state. captures this class of regression early.

maya: agreed. created a small dashboard widget and a pager rule on canary only for now.

infra-bot: deploy report — canary: prefetch-throttle rollout v2 started at 1902348000, 6 pods updated, no deploy failures.

maya: next steps: 1) Zoe to land bucketed freelist PR + microbench, 2) Sanjiv to add workspace_reallocs metric/alert, 3) Liam to run extended 7d canary with combined patch, 4) I'll coordinate rollback policy and docs. targeting PRs by EOD tomorrow.

liam: I'll schedule the 7d run. tagging @oncall for FYI.

zoe: will open PR and include a small feature flag for safe rollback.

maya: thanks all. leaving notes in the perf run doc and will follow up with flamegraphs in the morning. :white_check_mark:
